documents.title: H&P - Admission - Sepsis, suspected urinary source
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of note: 06:10, HD1
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Fever, chills, flank pain x 2 days.
HPI:
50 yo F presents to ED via private vehicle with 2 days of dysuria, urinary frequency, then rigors and R flank pain overnight.
Arrived ED 02:10. Reports 2 episodes of emesis, poor oral intake since yesterday afternoon, felt lightheaded on standing.
No cough, no dyspnea at rest, no diarrhea, no rash, no abdominal surgery, no recent instrumentation.
Denies vaginal discharge. LMP approx 3 wks ago, no pregnancy concern reported.
Daughter at bedside confirms pt was well until 2 days ago and is normally independent, works full time.
Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200 on initial CBC.
Pt became progressively more tachycardic and hypotensive during ED course as below.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes, diet and metformin controlled. Hypertension. Recurrent UTI (2 in past year). Iron deficiency anemia.
No prior ICU admission. No known CKD, baseline renal function normal.
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
Cholecystectomy, remote. C-section x1.
HOME MEDICATIONS
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily
Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily
ALLERGIES
Sulfa - rash.
SOCIAL / FAMILY
Lives with husband and son. Nonsmoker. Rare alcohol. No drug use. Family hx: mother with DM2.
ED COURSE
02:10 - hypotensive and febrile appearing. Sepsis pathway activated. 2 large bore IVs placed.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
02:20 - blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field, positive nitrite, many bacteria, 3+ blood.
02:45 - Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added for empiric coverage given hypotension.
Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77. Second liter started after transient improvement.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
04:50 - Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65. Right IJ central line placed.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO for fever. Foley placed for strict I/O.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive: fever, chills, dysuria, flank pain, nausea, lightheadedness, myalgias.
Negative: chest pain, orthopnea, hemoptysis, melena, focal weakness, neck stiffness, photophobia.
PHYSICAL EXAM
Gen: ill appearing, diaphoretic, answers appropriately.
Vitals at exam 06:00: T 38.2 C, HR 104, BP 98/61 on norepinephrine, RR 22, SpO2 96% on 2 L NC.
HEENT: mucous membranes dry, no scleral icterus, no oral lesions.
Neck: supple, no JVD, no meningismus.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, cap refill 3 sec.
Pulm: clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, R CVA tenderness marked, mild suprapubic tenderness, no rebound or guarding, BS present.
Ext: warm, no edema, no calf tenderness.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae. Neuro: oriented x3, no focal deficit.
LABS / IMAGING
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
BUN 34, Na 133, K 4.1, HCO3 18, glucose 214, AST 38, ALT 30, T bili 1.4, INR 1.2.
Hgb 10.8, MCV 78. Procalcitonin elevated. Trop negative x1.
CXR: no infiltrate, no effusion. CT abd/pelvis w/o contrast deferred pending renal function; renal US shows no hydronephrosis.
ASSESSMENT / PLAN
50 yo F with septic shock, source most consistent with acute pyelonephritis/complicated UTI, with AKI and thrombocytopenia.
1. Septic shock - vasopressor per above, MAP goal >65, wean as tolerated. Repeat lactate q6h. Strict I/O.
2. Infection - continue broad spectrum IV antibiotics, narrow when culture data return. Follow up sensitivities.
3. AKI - hold lisinopril and metformin, avoid nephrotoxins, trend BMP q12h, monitor urine output hourly.
4. Thrombocytopenia - likely sepsis related, recheck CBC in AM, no anticoagulation for now, SCDs for VTE prophylaxis.
5. Glycemic control - SSI q6h, hold home oral agents.
6. Dispo - ICU admission, family updated at 06:05. Full code.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 07:20 - Septic shock, pyelonephritis
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
SUBJECTIVE
Pt awake, feels better than overnight. Flank pain 4/10, down from 8/10. Tolerated ice chips. No chills since 03:00.
OVERNIGHT EVENTS
Norepinephrine weaned from 0.12 to 0.04 mcg/kg/min by 06:00 with MAP 70-78. Total 3.2 L crystalloid since arrival.
Urine output 45-60 mL/hr over last 6 hrs, improved from 15 mL/hr.
Remained on IV antibiotics overnight, no infusion reactions.
VITALS
T max 38.3 C, T now 37.6 C, HR 92, BP 106/65, RR 18, SpO2 97% on 1 L NC.
EXAM
Gen: less diaphoretic. Cardiac: RRR, no murmur. Pulm: clear. Abd: soft, R CVA tenderness improved, no guarding.
Ext: trace pedal edema. Neuro: alert, oriented x3.
Central line site clean, no erythema.
LABS
Creatinine 2.1, BUN 30, K 3.9, HCO3 21. WBC 13,400. Platelets 79,000. Hgb 10.2.
Lactate 1.9 at 06:00. Blood and urine cultures pending.
ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Septic shock, resolving - continue norepinephrine wean, goal off by afternoon, MAP >65.
2. Complicated UTI/pyelonephritis - continue current antibiotic regimen pending culture results.
3. AKI - improving, creatinine trending down, continue to hold ACEi and metformin, no NSAIDs.
4. Thrombocytopenia - stable, recheck in AM, no bleeding.
5. Nutrition - advance to clear liquids. SSI continues, CBG 148-190.
6. Foley to remain while on pressors, remove once off.
7. Transfer to step-down when vasopressor free x 4 hrs. Daughter updated 07:10.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 16:40 - culture data, off pressors
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 16:40 (interval/afternoon)
INTERVAL EVENTS
Norepinephrine off at 13:15. MAP 72-84 off support x 3.5 hrs, no rebound hypotension with sitting up.
Micro called at 08:20 with growth in aerobic bottles; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours, sensitivities pending.
Vancomycin discontinued at 09:00 per attending given gram negative growth and no MRSA risk factors.
Continued piperacillin-tazobactam IV, next dose 18:00.
Foley removed 14:00, voided 220 mL spontaneously at 16:10.
VITALS 16:30
INTAKE/OUTPUT
In 1.8 L, out 1.35 L since 07:00. Net positive 4.1 L for admission.
EXAM
Gen: comfortable, sitting up in chair. Cardiac: RRR. Pulm: clear bilaterally. Abd: soft, minimal R CVA tenderness.
No rash, no purpura. Ambulated to door with RN, steady.
LABS PM
Creatinine 1.6, BUN 24, HCO3 23. Platelets 96,000. WBC 9,800. Lactate 1.3 at 14:00.
ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Septic shock secondary to E. coli urinary source - shock resolved, off vasopressor. Monitor for recurrence.
2. Antibiotics - continue IV therapy, plan to tailor to oral agent once susceptibilities available.
3. AKI - improving with resolution of shock, repeat BMP in AM, resume home lisinopril only after creatinine near baseline.
4. Thrombocytopenia - recovering as expected with source control.
5. Transfer out of ICU this evening to medical floor, telemetry.
6. PT eval ordered. Anticipate discharge HD3 if afebrile and eating.
7. Central line to be removed on floor in AM if peripheral access adequate. Husband updated at 16:35.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3 - E. coli urosepsis with AKI
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: 3 days, discharged HD3 at 15:20.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES
1. Septic shock due to E. coli complicated urinary tract infection / acute pyelonephritis, resolved.
2. Acute kidney injury, resolving.
3. Sepsis associated thrombocytopenia, recovering.
4. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. 5. Hypertension.
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
50 yo F presented at 02:10 with 2 days of dysuria and flank pain, rigors, hypotension. Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.

Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77. Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65; weaned off HD2 at 13:15.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 on admission.
Vancomycin stopped HD2 once gram negative organism identified. Urine culture grew same organism, pan-sensitive.
Renal function improved with volume resuscitation and source control; central line and Foley removed prior to discharge.
Afebrile >24 hrs at discharge, ambulating, tolerating regular diet.
DISCHARGE VITALS / LABS
Creatinine 1.2, BUN 18, K 4.0, WBC 7,600, platelets 128,000, Hgb 10.5.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
Cephalexin 500 mg PO QID x 7 days (per susceptibilities).
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID - resume now.
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily - hold until follow up labs reviewed.
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain or fever.
FOLLOW UP
Primary care in 5-7 days for BMP and blood pressure check, discuss restarting lisinopril.
Urology referral for recurrent UTI evaluation.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS
Complete full antibiotic course. Drink 2 L fluid daily unless told otherwise.
Return for fever above 38.0 C, rigors, vomiting, inability to urinate, lightheadedness, or worsening flank pain.
No driving while on pain medication. Gradual return to work in 1 week.
Instructions reviewed with pt and daughter at bedside, teach back completed. Discharged home ambulatory with family.
